incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a misconfigured GitHub Actions workflow (pull_request_target) to steal the asyncapi-bot publishing token, then rode the project's trusted-publishing pipeline to release five poisoned npm package versions carrying an import-time loader.
incidents.impact: Trojanized @asyncapi/specs, generator, generator-helpers, and generator-components versions fetched the Miasma RAT from IPFS on import, spawning a hidden persistent process; credential-harvesting modules were present but disabled in this build. Any workstation, CI/CD pipeline, or build that resolved the versions during the ~90-minute window was exposed.

incidents.vector: A single threat group chained two zero-days - a maximum-severity authentication bypass (CVE-2026-15409) and an authenticated command-injection flaw (CVE-2026-15410) - to fully compromise internet-facing SMA1000 VPN appliances.
incidents.impact: Active in-the-wild exploitation observed since June 22 with assessed ransomware intent; both CVEs added to the CISA KEV catalog on July 14. Patches shipped July 14 but SonicWall warns patching alone is insufficient and compromise should be assumed.

incidents.vector: FSB Center 16 operators scan internet-exposed routers for weak SNMP community strings, issue SNMP Set-Requests to copy device configurations, and exfiltrate them via TFTP; they also exploit older Cisco vulnerabilities and Smart Install.
incidents.impact: A Five Eyes and EU joint advisory details a decade-plus campaign compromising poorly configured routers to gain persistent access across multiple critical infrastructure sectors globally, including Australia and the US.

incidents.victim: Organizations running on-premises Microsoft SharePoint Server
incidents.vector: Threat actors chained three remote-code-execution flaws (CVE-2026-32201, CVE-2026-45659, CVE-2026-56164) against internet-facing SharePoint, then stole IIS machine keys and abused deserialization for persistence.
incidents.impact: CISA warned of active exploitation of on-prem SharePoint (Subscription Edition, 2019, 2016) with webshell deployment, machine-key theft, and malware; all three CVEs are on the KEV catalog, the last added the day of the alert.

incidents.vector: NetNut, operated by Israeli firm Alarum Technologies, distributed SDKs bundled into smart TVs, streaming boxes, and mobile apps that silently enrolled home devices as always-on proxy exit nodes with little or no consent.
incidents.impact: The FBI, IRS-CI, Google, Lumen, and Shadowserver disrupted the network of at least 2 million devices - used for scraping, ad fraud, account takeover, and to mask 316 distinct threat clusters in one week - seizing hundreds of NetNut domains.

incidents.vector: Three St. Petersburg nationals ran Media Land and ML Cloud, providing bulletproof hosting and technical support designed to help cybercriminals evade law enforcement.
incidents.impact: DOJ unsealed an indictment against Aleksandr Volosovik (alias 'Yalishanda'), Yulia Pankova, and Kirill Zatolokin whose infrastructure served LockBit, BlackSuit, and Play ransomware and multiple carding forums; a $10M State Department reward was offered, though the defendants remain in Russia.

incidents.victim: US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor published 844 MB of sensitive data to a public GitHub repository, including a file of AWS GovCloud admin credentials and a CSV of plaintext usernames and passwords for dozens of internal systems.
incidents.impact: Credentials sat exposed for roughly six months while CISA ignored nine automated GitGuardian alerts and took over 48 hours to rotate keys after notification; no known malicious exploitation was reported.

incidents.victim: US property owners with active permit applications
incidents.vector: An organized ring (tracked as 'Diligent Planner') pulls public permit records, emails property owners while impersonating planning departments with accurate property details, and pressures wire, P2P, or crypto payments against a deadline.
incidents.impact: Researchers linked 53 verified money-mule accounts across 23 campaigns; the activity sits within a government-impersonation fraud category whose 2025 US losses roughly doubled to ~$798M, and the FBI's IC3 issued a public alert.

incidents.victim: US businesses, hospitals, and municipal governments
incidents.vector: The First VPN Service (1VPNS) sold bulletproof anonymity infrastructure to ransomware operators to hide attack origins, deploy malware, and manage exfiltrated data.
incidents.impact: OFAC, alongside the UK, sanctioned 1VPNS and alleged operators Dmytro Rashevskyi and Yegeniy Silayev; the service had supported ransomware families including Anubis and Sinobi and followed a May Europol takedown.

incidents.victim: Internet-connected security cameras near NATO and Ukraine military routes
incidents.vector: Russian intelligence scans the internet for exposed IP cameras, exploits weak or default credentials and outdated firmware, then applies AI image recognition to identify military vehicles and cargo.
incidents.impact: A Dutch AIVD/MIVD advisory warned that hacked camera feeds in the Netherlands, other NATO states, and Ukraine are used to track military logistics and Ukraine-bound weapons shipments, with intel in Ukraine supporting lethal strikes on personnel.

incidents.vector: Attackers accessed a customer database that was stored separately and maintained by a third-party IT service provider, briefly opening the file and exfiltrating part of its contents.
incidents.impact: Stolen data included names, phone numbers, emails, dates of birth, and customer numbers; Lidl says no passwords, addresses, or payment data were taken and its own shopping platform was unaffected, but warned customers of phishing risk.

incidents.victim: Website owners globally, including many Australian SMBs
incidents.vector: Mass scanning and exploitation of roughly 17 known CMS and plugin vulnerabilities (unauthenticated file upload, RCE, SSRF, deserialization) to deploy webshells, with AI accelerating exploitation speed.
incidents.impact: ACSC issued a critical alert on webshell-based remote control of compromised web servers enabling credential theft, malware hosting, and pivoting to broader network compromise; many small and medium Australian businesses were impacted.

incidents.victim: UK Foreign Office, British embassies, and local councils
incidents.vector: A threat actor using the handle 'SantaAd' claimed the 'FortiBleed' campaign, harvesting firewall and VPN credentials from roughly 80,000 Fortinet devices.
incidents.impact: Credentials tied to the UK Foreign Office, British embassies, and some local councils are being sold as a single archive for $60,000.

incidents.vector: A malicious governance action redirected 4.4 trillion BONK tokens to attacker-controlled wallets.
incidents.impact: About $20M in crypto-assets were stolen, prompting Upbit and Kraken to pause BONK transactions while the theft is investigated.

incidents.vector: A pro-Kurdish group defaced multiple US Army websites.
incidents.impact: Sites were defaced with messages attacking Donald Trump and the US Ambassador to Turkiye Tom Barrack.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into a cloud-based platform, tied by reporting to a broader hacking spree exploiting the Oracle PeopleSoft platform.
incidents.impact: The intruder accessed patient data and internal documents, then contacted the company on June 15; AdaptHealth disclosed the breach to the SEC and investors.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion and ransomware deployment by a newly launched operation calling itself 'Settra'.
incidents.impact: One of Taiwan's largest mobile operators was hacked; the company says its mobile payments platform was unaffected, and Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs opened an investigation into possible data theft.

incidents.vector: Operators affiliated with Alibaba and its Qwen AI lab used 25,000+ fraudulent accounts to generate 28.8 million exchanges (April 22-June 5) to distill Claude's outputs and train competing models.
incidents.impact: Anthropic told US lawmakers this 'largest known distillation attack' accelerates Chinese AI and cyber capabilities benefiting the PLA; separately, Alibaba banned employees from using Claude after finding user-tracking code.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion by the Cyber Anarchy Squad, which wiped systems and destroyed backups.
incidents.impact: The group claimed wiping 3,000 servers and workstations plus 700 virtual machines, deleting all backups, and stealing over 650 TB of documents from one of Russia's largest construction firms.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion into Kubota's North American environment.
incidents.impact: A breach between March and April 2026 exposed employee information; no group has claimed responsibility.

incidents.vector: Intrusion deploying novel ransomware with a previously unseen encryption algorithm; no ransom note was left.
incidents.impact: Newly reported attribution ties the September-October 2025 attack that shut JLR production lines to Russia-based hackers; the incident is Britain's most costly ever at an estimated GBP 1.9B (US$2.55B), with a measurable hit to UK GDP.
